si_4_title.answer: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities unveil two neuroanatomical obsessive-compulsive disorder subtypes

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study uses a local dataset from Zhengzhou University (100 OCD, 106 HC) and an external single-site dataset (Southwest University, 492 HC) for structural covariance network construction.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We recruited 100 untreated, first-episode OCD patients and 106 healthy controls..." (Zhengzhou); "The normal structural covariance network was constructed using another extensive dataset from a single site, comprising 492 healthy individuals..." (Southwest)
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Wen2025.pdf.md: Methods / Participants; Methods / Disease epicenter mapping for each subtype

answer.SINGLE-SITE: normative training for gray matter volume model (Zhengzhou University dataset); structural covariance network construction (Southwest University dataset)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The Zhengzhou University dataset (106 HCs) was used to train the normative model for gray matter volume. The Southwest University dataset (492 HCs) was used to construct a normal structural covariance network for epicenter mapping.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional GMVs from age and sex in HCs..." (Zhengzhou); "The normal structural covariance network was constructed using another extensive dataset from a single site..." (Southwest)
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Wen2025.pdf.md: Methods / Subtyping analysis based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities; Methods / Disease epicenter mapping for each subtype
